title: I Used the Sprung-Floor Hours on the Coach Who Camped My Numbered Marley

parts.text: I stepped into studio A at 2:06 p.m. and coach Tamsin was already using my numbered marley. The board said: NINETY MINUTES. MARLEY STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty, floor steward, holding a clipboard that listed our tap. Tamsin shrugged. "Coaches keep the floor." I photographed the board, the booking, and her taps on my marley. Then I asked for the floor hours. At 2:14 the studio desk pinged why Tamsin's taps sat on our marley. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio desk can see Tamsin's taps in studio A during our ninety minutes.

social.video_title: She camped my numbered marley — Part 1/2
social.description: Sprung floor, a coach on my marley, a ninety-minute clock she posted. I logged the taps. Would you have asked for the floor hours?

parts.text: Tamsin called it across-the-floor until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the marley still. The marley went back to my numbered roll. Tamsin ran a slot of their own and told the next coach atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: COACHES DO NOT KEEP THE FLOOR. I keep our tap on a labeled card. Tamsin brown-bags her taps. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches do not keep the floor — Part 2/2
social.description: Floor hours, numbered marley, and a second line on the board. Was across-the-floor ever our tap?
